thread:
erin: Heads up from support: customers in the route-eval canary see inconsistent "effective permissions" for routes during heavy config churn. Example: tenant `nova` preview says `quota:override=false` even though role lists it. This blocks quota edits in the console.
vlad: timeline? Did this start after the recent routing-policies merge?
erin: started ~09:12 UTC after we flipped the route-eval V2 for 30% of tenants. Happened while SRE ran a config push for routing affinity.
tina: quick diagnosis: route-eval V2 reads from the materialized `rbac_flat_view` for speed. The merger job that populates the view lags under bursty writes; we observed ~20-40s windows where view is stale.
marta: UX impact is bad. For console users, we should either: 1) surface a clear temporary notice allowing edits with confirmation, or 2) fall back to an authoritative read so the UI is correct. Thoughts?
vlad: fallback seems right: for any role preview request, if `view_age_ms > 10000` then route-eval should do a read-through to primary store (roles service) for that tenant+route. That avoids letting stale reads block user action.
erin: read-through will add latency to preview calls in some cases. Can we make that conditional only when the computed result differs from the stored role? But detecting difference requires another read, so might be double-read anyway.
tina: propose this flow: 1) route-eval queries materialized view and returns result + header `X-View-Age-ms`. 2) console inspects header; if >10000 show a small "stale read" badge and enable an "Ensure fresh" button that calls `GET /api/v1/roles/:id/preview?fresh=true`. 3) `fresh=true` forces route-eval to read from primary store. This moves the latency to an explicit user action and is safer.
marta: I like explicit action. UX will be: greyed edit controls with a small link "results might be stale - ensure fresh" which when clicked shows spinner then refreshes payload and unblocks edits. No surprise edits.
erin: also need telemetry: `perm_preview.view_age_ms` histogram, `perm_preview.fresh_click` counter, and `perm_preview.result_mismatch` boolean so we can quantify how often materialized view mismatches primary store.
ops-bot: noted. We'll schedule an infra job to temporarily increase merger frequency for the canary cohort for the next 3 hours to reduce impact while patch lands.
vlad: implementation plan: route-eval: add `X-View-Age-ms` in response; support `?fresh=true` to force primary read; add a fast path that if `view_age_ms <= 100` returns immediately. Also emit telemetry events.
tina: console changes: show inline badge when header present and >10s, add "Ensure fresh" button calling `?fresh=true`, and show a brief info tooltip about canary. Put banner behind `showPreviewFreshButton` feature flag first.
marta: test plan: unit tests for route-eval fresh path, integration test that simulates merger lag, telemetry assertions, and manual canary verification with tenant `nova` and `beta-inc`. Also update runbook: support should be instructed to hit the Ensure fresh button and capture `X-View-Age-ms` when filed.
erin: small ask: add an admin console action to trigger an on-demand merge for a tenant (manual sync) behind `allowManualMerge` ent. Support can trigger for customers during incidents.
vlad: database owners worried about adding manual merges but ok as admin-only behind a feature flag + rate limit. We'll add an audit entry `manual_merge.requested_by` and emit `rbac.merge.manual` telemetry.
ops-bot: deploy queued for staging (build #8111) - running unit + integration suites.
marta: tagging @sre for visibility on increased merger frequency. Vlad, include a performance guard: if merger time > 200ms per tenant, revert frequency bump.
vlad: Will do. I'll open PRs: 1) route-eval: header + ?fresh=true + telemetry + docs; 2) console: badge + ensure fresh button + admin manual merge UI; 3) runbook + dashboard panels for `perm_preview.*`.
tina: after merge let's run a 2-hour canary: flip route-eval V2 for 10 tenants and monitor `perm_preview.result_mismatch` and support tickets.
marta: great. Thanks team.
